[[File:Smuggler_Chick_with_Sword_FC.png|thumb|right|250px|A [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] scoundrel]]
{{Quote|You like me because I'm a scoundrel. There aren't enough scoundrels in your life.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="Episode 5">{{Film|V}}</ref>}}
'''Scoundrels''' were individuals considered to be rogues by the [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] mainstream society. They often lived outside the law or actively fought against it. 

==Description==
Scoundrels were [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] rogues, operating outside the bounds of law or attempting to circumvent it in order to enrich themselves. Hailing from any [[Planet/Legends|world]] or region in the galaxy, scoundrels usually did not intend to find themselves in a position to defy authority or live on the wrong side of the law. In most cases, they were thrust into the world through poor [[Lady Luck/Legends|luck]], bad decisions, or being swept along in circumstances beyond their control.<ref name="RPG-Core">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook]]''</ref>

Scoundrels lived a life of adventure; they had many reasons for leading the life they did. Some scoundrels were good-[[Heart/Legends|hearted]] rogues, often searching for adventure and excitement, or to right a wrong someone did to them or a loved one. Others had darker reasons, seeking to advance their own criminal careers or to satisfy their greed for [[Currency/Legends|money]] and power. Most scoundrels found a middle ground, remaining fluid in their allegiance and taking advantage of [[Politics/Legends|political]] shifts as needed. The term scoundrel encompassed a wide variety of occupations, including [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]], [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], outlaws, [[Gambler/Legends|gamblers]], [[Slicer/Legends|slicers]], [[Con artist/Legends|con artists]], [[Thief/Legends|thieves]], and [[Spy/Legends|spies]].<ref name="RPG-Core" />

Relying on their intelligence, charisma, and dexterity, scoundrels had a penchant for getting themselves in and out of trouble. Quick-witted with sharp reflexes, they possessed a strong self-preservation instinct that helped to keep them alive, but they also found themselves at the mercy of their own need to experience the thrill of their chosen profession. Scoundrels lived by their wits, full of bravado and possessed of a number of skills that took advantage of their innate cunning. They often attempted to talk their way out of trouble, but they were also accomplished liars and cheats, and were comfortable deceiving, tricking, and stealing as the need arose.<ref name="RPG-Core" />

Experienced scoundrels could tell when trouble was brewing, and often preferred to avoid it rather than face it head on. However, they were capable fighters, and scoundrels liked to take advantage of sneak attacks in combat.<ref name="RPG-Core" />

==History==
During the years of the [[Great Galactic War]] and the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] that followed it circa [[3653 BBY]], the term scoundrel referred to a particular breed of [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] who fought for the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. These scoundrels were known for their unpredictability, skill, and underhandedness in combat.<ref name="HoloSmug">{{Holonet|classes|smuggler|Smuggler}}</ref> During the last years of the [[Great Peace of the Republic|"Great Peace" of the Republic]], [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] told [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], who was considering leaving the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], that he could not expect himself, as one man, to fix a galaxy he defined as being full of scoundrels. Unaware that he was being manipulated into eventually becoming Palpatine's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]], Dooku bluntly told Palpatine that the believed one man, if powerful enough, should be able to stand against those scoundrels.<ref name="SWDP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:ChissScoundrel-TUR.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A female [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] scoundrel]]
The term "scoundrel" was first referred to in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']] when [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Princess Leia]] admits to [[Han Solo]] that she considers him all right when he's not "acting like a scoundrel". Han likes this description, the encounter leading the couple to kiss.<ref name="Episode 5" />

Scoundrel was one the eight starting classes established in the [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook|Core Rulebook]] for [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]''. [[Deel Surool]], a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]], served as the character example for the class.<ref name="RPG-Core" />

The scoundrel is a hero class in the [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]] and the ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'' video games. The class is characterized by having many skill points, but very few Vitality Points or Feats. The class also receives the "Sneak Attack" and "Scoundrel's Luck" line of feats for free. While sneak attack focuses on increased damage for a stealth-based opening attack, "Scoundrel's Luck" passively increases their defense points allowing for higher dodge chances. Many consider it to be an "expert class." The [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Revised Core Rulebook]] grants scoundrels similar abilities.

In ''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic'' the scoundrel is one of the three non-Jedi starting classes (alongside [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] and [[Scout/Legends|scout]]) that the player could choose.

The scoundrel is an advanced class for the smuggler class in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' MMO video game. This advanced class can specialize in Scrapper, Sawbones (healing), or [[Unarmed combat/Legends|dirty fighting]], the use of a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]], [[Scatter gun/Legends|Scatter gun]], [[Stealth field generator/Legends|stealth]], and [[Medpac/Legends|combat medicine]].<ref name="HoloSmug" /> The [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Imperial]] counterpart for this archetype is the [[operative]].<ref name="Fan Friday">{{TORweb|url=news/news-article/20100820-0|text=STAR WARS: The Old Republic Fan Friday (August 20, 2010)|nolive=1}}</ref>
